source: Http3ConnectionWriteStallWatcher times the request streams of one QUIC connection together: holderBytes is half the smaller of the client's initial_max_data and initial_max_stream_data_bidi_local (Http3StreamWriteStallHandler.holderBytes, from the peer's transport parameters), so a stream sent less than that, here one waiting on connection credit a stalled stream holds, is spared when the holder is reset and completes once the credit comes back; only the holder is reset and counted

steps.note: one connection granted 96 KiB (holderBytes 48 KiB) and nothing more for 4.9 s: a 200 KB response takes all of it and is reset at the check 3 s later (checks every second from its first wait); a small response on a second stream, 50 ms behind it and so also overdue there, waits on that credit, is spared for 2.5 s at the reset, and is served whole once credit returns (at the reset for quinn, which frees what a reset stream held; at the end of the stall for aioquic)
one HTTP/3 stream reset, the holder
